description: What the fleet must serve. Traffic shape comes from an inference-perf workload-catalog entry or the user's own inference-perf config; this spec adds only rate, tenants with SLOs, objective, budget and constraints.

workload.description: Exactly one of catalog_entry, inference_perf_config, trace, agentx.

catalog_entry.description: An entry of kubernetes-sigs/inference-perf/workload-catalog, vendored at the pinned ref.

inference_perf_config.description: Path to a user-supplied inference-perf config YAML, including trace replay configs built from request logs.

trace.description: Reserved: a request log to turn into a replay config. Not supported yet; convert it to an inference-perf trace config first.

target_qps.description: The aggregate request rate the SLOs are a promise about.

data.description: Deep-merged over the workload source's `data` block before the benchmark runs. Use it to fit a catalog entry to the server (for example cap dynamic_system_prompt_len.max below max_model_len) without forking the entry; the merged block is recorded in the release so a report says what was actually sent.

agentx.description: The SemiAnalysis InferenceX AgentX benchmark: aiperf's `inferencex-agentx-mvp` scenario replaying the public agentic-coding traces in closed loop at a fixed number of concurrent sessions. The suite runs the exact aiperf command InferenceX's benchmark_lib.sh builds (pin 754356e9) and reduces the export with InferenceX's formulas, so a point is the number the submission pipeline would compute. Ranking is total tok/s per chip; the qualifying gate defaults to TTFT p50 <= 5 s (tenancy[].slo overrides).

concurrency.description: The ladder of points: a list of integers (InferenceX's conc-list, e.g. [8,16,24,32,48,64,80,96]) or {start, step, max}. The search climbs along it; a submission sweep measures all of it.

dataset.description: HF dataset id behind the loader when it is not one the pins know.

duration_s.description: Seconds per point (default 3600; 1200 in fast mode). Below 900 aiperf needs --unsafe-override and the point is not submission-valid.

fast.description: InferenceX's AIPERF_EXPERIMENTAL_FAST: 1200 s and one warm-up request per lane. For search rounds, not for the submission sweep.

served_model_name.description: The name the front door serves the model under when it differs from the recipe's model (aiperf --model).

tokenizer.description: HF tokenizer id for aiperf (default: the recipe's tokenizer, then its model).

max_context_length.description: aiperf --max-context-length; unset replays the whole corpus as the TPU recipe does.

aiperf_ref.description: aiperf commit to install (default: the InferenceX submodule pin).

share.description: Fraction of target_qps this tenant sends. Shares sum to 1.

priority.description: Higher is more important; negative is sheddable under burst. Read by flow control once that arm exists.

slo.description: Keys of the form <ttft|tpot|itl|e2e>_p<50|90|99>_ms. Defaults to the catalog entry's metadata.slos when omitted.

primary_metric.description: The one number verdicts are computed on. Both are always reported. cost_per_1M_tokens_at_slo needs budget.chip_hour_cost. AgentX workloads rank on total_tokens_per_s_per_chip (default) or output_tokens_per_s_per_chip; the goodput metrics do not apply to a closed-loop replay.

target.description: Optional stopping target on the primary metric. Without it the objective is to attain the SLO at target_qps and keep improving until the search converges.

max_chip_hours.description: Study-wide spend bound; the stopping rule's chip-hour clause.

search.description: How far the search may go past the fleet.

engine_loop.description: When the fleet search plateaus with the objective unmet, hand the bound role to tpu-performance and come back with the improved recipe.
